newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. aid to hurricane victims delayed by red tape.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aid to hurricane victims delayed by red tape.

text.p: A planeload of aid for victims of Hurricane Lili sent last Saturday by mostly Cuban American donors in the United States was still in a warehouse in the capital on Wednesday, apparently delayed by red tape.

Father Thomas Wenski, an official of Miami Roman Catholic archdiocese that channelled the aid to a Cuban church charity, said the cargo of some 30 tonnes of rice, beans and milk had not yet been transported to central city of Cienfuegos, where it is meant to be distributed.
"We're still working on some very delicate negotiations," Wenski told Reuters.

He did not give details of what was holding things up, but admitted that one problem had been that some of the milk sent in the cargo had been inscribed by donors with messages such as "exile" and "love can do everything".
"We tried to explain to authorities that they (donors) did not do this with bad intentions, that it was not done to provoke," said Wenski.

However, he added this was not the main reason for the delays, explaining authorities were sorting through the milk because it was in various forms -- such as powdered, tinned and low-fat -- and had to be checked by sanitary officials.
"But it (this problem) shouldn't have complicated things this much," Wenski said.

The aid was donated to the Cuban church charity Caritas for distribution to people worst affected by Hurricane Lili. Authorities have said the storm, which swept central and western areas of Cuba on Oct. 17-18, destroyed some 5,000 homes and damaged crops, power lines and communications.

The Cuban American community in Florida moblized rapdily to send aid, although some hardline critics of President Fidel Castro argued against sending anything, saying assistance would just serve to prop up the government.

The church in Miami has more aid ready and had planned another flight on Sunday. But Wenski said this might now not be possible since church officials wanted to get Saturday's cargo distributed first.
The U.S. government last week waived a ban on direct flights from the United States to the communist-ruled island in order to allow the relief flight to take place.
